basis: Hemolytic anemia with Heinz bodies directly affects red blood cells.
BCR-ABL1-positive myeloid neoplasm affects marrow and blood; common splenic involvement remains within the haematologic axis.
Severe insulin resistance, hyperinsulinemia and androgen excess define the endocrine disorder; persistent acanthosis nigricans is part of its defining triad.
Mast-cell lineage neoplasm; persistent cutaneous mast-cell infiltration occurs in well over 30% across common forms. Other organ damage varies substantially by subtype.
Defined by impaired cognitive function, including dementia and delirium; cognitive disorders fall within the neurologic axis despite the psychiatric parent.
ALS subtype with motor-neuron degeneration and polyglucosan bodies; muscle wasting from denervation does not establish primary muscle disease.
Neoplasms arise in ovarian reproductive tissue; no common direct involvement of a covered organ is established.
Mitochondrial metabolic disease defined by cerebellar ataxia and neuropathy; ophthalmoplegia is neurologic. Hashimoto thyroiditis is a separate autoimmune diagnosis.
Acquired elevation of red-cell concentration or mass; underlying hypoxia or erythropoietin-producing disorders are causes, not additional affected organs.
Carcinoma in situ originates in the gastric epithelium.
Microcephaly and developmental impairment define disease; thyroid hormone deficiency occurs in 2/5 (40%), supporting endocrine dysfunction. Celiac disease is a separate diagnosis.
Myoepithelial tumors most commonly arise in salivary glands, within the gastrointestinal axis; breast and soft-tissue origins are site-specific variants of this umbrella.
IRF5-associated inflammatory bowel disease causes immune-mediated intestinal inflammation; extraintestinal damage is not established as common.
Striatal degeneration directly impairs basal-ganglia function, producing rigidity and movement abnormalities.
Complex I metabolic defect; encephalopathy/cerebellar atrophy and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy each reported in 1/1 assessed. Tiny denominators limit certainty; optic atrophy 1-4% excluded.
Retinal capillary dysfunction and macular degeneration impair central vision; localized retinal vascular changes do not establish a separate cardiovascular disorder.
Defined by autoimmune injury to peripheral nerves or the neuromuscular junction; ocular injury is subtype-specific.
TULP1-associated inherited retinal degeneration causes severe visual dysfunction; cataracts and optic-disc changes remain within the ocular axis.
Echinococcal hydatid cysts directly occupy cardiac tissue and expand into a heart chamber; other infection sites are not established as common in this concept.
Microcephaly and severe developmental disability define disease; scoliosis occurs in 30-79%. Characteristic cry alone does not establish lasting airway damage; heart defects occur in 5-29%.
Although arising in the prostate, clinical BPH directly compresses the urethra and impairs urinary outflow; urethral and bladder function belong to the renal axis.
Flat intraepithelial neoplasia originates in urinary bladder urothelium.
FGFR1-rearranged hematopoietic neoplasm affects marrow and blood; lymphoma is one presentation rather than a defining feature across this heterogeneous group.
Neoplasm of the uterine cervix, a reproductive organ outside the axes; infection is not intrinsic to every subtype.
Restrictive cardiomyopathy directly impairs myocardial filling; systemic deposition, inflammation and other organ injury depend on the underlying subtype.
